subject: Azure Private Offer — multi-year commitment phasing, credits & ramp ops
messages:
From: Tom Hines <tom.hines@microsoft.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Lina Sørensen <lina.sorensen@brightline.ai>
Date: 2027-05-11T09:12:00+02:00
Subject: Azure private offer — initial commitment phasing proposal

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the time earlier. Per our call, attaching an initial term-sheet for a private offer scoped to Brightline AI. Key points below — this is meant to be a starting point for negotiation rather than final legal language.

Quick summary:
- 3-year nominal commitment with annual prepay (Year 1 / Year 2 / Year 3)
- Step-down discount schedule tied to committed APUs (annual purchase units): 18% Yr1 / 16% Yr2 / 14% Yr3
- True-up window: 60 days post-year-end; overages billed at the effective discounted rate for that year
- Migration credit: one-time 5% credit applied in Year 1 for Marketplace onboarding activities
- Optional staircase feature: ability to accelerate prepay into a higher tranche mid-year with pro‑rated discount benefit

I've attached pricing_grid_v2.xlsx and a term summary PDF (private_offer_term_sheet.pdf). If Brightline prefers a flat multi-year prepay (single payment at signing) we can run alternate numbers — that typically buys ~3–4% incremental discount on top of the Yr1 rate above.

Questions for you / Brightline procurement:
1) Do you need side letter language for data residency/audit?
2) Is a 60-day true-up cadence acceptable?
3) Would you consider a compressed ramp (50% Yr1 consumption expected) or do you want the baseline we modeled (30% Yr1 / 35% Yr2 / 35% Yr3)?

If that looks directionally OK I can generate a DocuSign private offer link and include the marketplace listing.

Best,
Tom
Account Executive — Microsoft Azure Marketplace
Attachments: pricing_grid_v2.xlsx (Excel), private_offer_term_sheet.pdf (PDF)
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T10:08:00+02:00
Subject: Fwd: Azure private offer — initial commitment phasing proposal

Forwarding Tom's note — Brightline asked us to get clarity on the discount cadence and the operational mechanics for the true-up and staircase prepay option. High-level asks from procurement attached in the HubSpot ticket.

My quick take: 60-day true-up seems tight but workable; we should push for 90 days if Brightline has complex invoicing. The migration credit is fine but I'd like to cap the staircase acceleration window to two calendar quarters to limit retro discounts.

Karthik / Marissa — can you review the pricing grid in the attachment and confirm:
- whether we can accept the proposed step-down rates (18/16/14) or whether we need to push to 19/17/15 to preserve target ARR?
- whether the compressed ramp scenario (50% Yr1) changes our recommended discount?

Thanks — I plan to respond to Tom by midday tomorrow with our counter and the preferred true-up window.

— Vanessa
Director, Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T08:33:00+02:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Azure private offer — initial commitment phasing proposal

Vanessa — quick notes after reviewing pricing_grid_v2.xlsx:

- Baseline math: the 18/16/14 schedule nets an average blended discount of ~16% over 3 years assuming the modeled ramp (30/35/35). If Brightline accelerates to 50% Yr1 the blended falls to ~17% (more favorable to customer).
- Ask: push Yr1 to 19% and keep Yr2/3 at 16/14? That gives us more buffer and still keeps the offer market-competitive in EU regions.
- True-up window: 90 days is reasonable; it reduces disputes for our finance team and gives Brightline extra time to reconcile consumption with internal chargebacks.
- Staircase: allow mid-year acceleration but limit to one election per contract year; pro-rate benefit based on remaining months and cap the incremental discount benefit to 2% extra relative to the current tranche. That prevents retroactive large credits.
- Migration credit: convert to a one-time credit applied as a reduction to the first invoice rather than a separate rebate to simplify bookkeeping.

I'll draft a short counter to Tom with these points and include suggested wording for the true-up and staircase clauses.

Karthik
Head of Revenue Operations
From: Tom Hines <tom.hines@microsoft.com>

Subject: Re: Azure private offer — counter proposal + DocuSign

Vanessa / Karthik / Lina — thanks for the quick review and the clear counter. We've updated the term sheet per your asks:
- Yr1/Yr2/Yr3: 19% / 16% / 14% (migration credit applied as first-invoice reduction)
- True-up window: 90 days post-year-end
- Staircase: single mid-year election allowed; pro-rated benefit; incremental discount cap = 2% relative to prior tranche

I've generated a DocuSign private offer and added the marketplace listing. Link below and attached a DocuSign cover note (docusign_private_offer_link.txt) for signatures.
